{"url":"https://github.com/Ljferrer/WorkAuditRefine/issues/1848","body":"## TL;DR

Issue recon across `/war-strategy` and campaign sessions reads **partial projections of issues** — `--json title,body` (comments silently excluded) piped through `head -40` (bodies silently truncated) — and the doctrine nowhere says an issue's comments are evidence. This just produced a live interview recommendation that **directly contradicted the operator's own comments on the issue it cited as its basis**, caught only by external review. This is a fourth leak shape for the authoring-side-verification charter: the **partial-source read** — consuming an evidence object's convenient projection while citing the whole object.

## The incident (2026-08-27, in-flight interview on #1731/#1838/#1845/#1846)

The interview's Q1 recommended the echo-round shape for re-audit-born absorbs as: *"Exactly ONE echo ace batch per task … its own re-audit may demote but NEVER funds a third round. Basis: #1731's own convergence sketch."*

#1731 carries two operator comments (SQPferrer, 2026-08-26T07:04 and 09:05) that overrule exactly that constraint:

> "It's not just a 'second' ace that I want. I want you to burn through the fix/ace→re-audit rounds **until you hit the limit** if it means fixing the problem on the spot rather than opening up a follow-up issue."

> "I don't care if you call it a `fix` round or an `ace` round or a `bisect` round. Just get it done. Fix what is broken when it is identified."

The body's "exactly ONE echo round" passage is an **illustrative sketch** ("e.g."); the comments are the **ruling** — operator provenance, later-dated, imperative. The recommendation cited the source while contradicting its highest-provenance content. External review caught it; the corrected design (budget-bounded re-entry: the ladder re-enters while `fixRounds < roundLimit − 2`; the reserve is the sole convergence rule) fell out immediately once the comments were read.

## The mined evidence (root cause is mechanical, not judgment)

From the campaign session ("Work audit refine campaign", transcript `c878d5da-ed5a-4614-8006-47e692e60042.jsonl` under the operator's `~/.claude/projects/…-authoring-side-verification-600a79/`), the **entire** recon read for this interview's issue set:

```bash
for n in 1846 1845 1838 1731 1664 1586 1552 1549 1547; do
  echo "===== #$n ====="
  gh issue view $n --repo Ljferrer/WorkAuditRefine --json title,body -q '"\(.title)\n\(.body)"' | head -40
done > "$S/enhancements.txt"
```

Three defects in one idiom:

1. **`--json title,body` silently excludes comments.** Nothing in the output marks their absence — a commented issue and an uncommented one render identically. (Bare `gh issue view` has the same default; comments require `--comments` or `--json …,comments`.)
2. **`| head -40` silently truncates bodies.** #1731's body exceeds 40 lines; its reconciliation points 4–5 (terminal-round siblings, regression posture) likely never entered context either. A truncated read renders as a complete one.
3. **Session-wide:** 152 commands, **zero comment reads**; the lone "comment" hit is a `gh issue comment` *write*.

So this is not an attention failure — the evidence was never fetched, and no doctrine required fetching it. The `authoring-side verification` recon lane (ADR 0044 amendment) enumerates corpus classes including "issue-linked artifacts" but never names **the issue's own comments** as part of the issue.

## Relation to existing doctrine

- **PIN-21 family, new species.** The charter's leak shapes cover the *unvalidated join-executor claim* (a mechanism cited as existing, unverified at the surface). The partial-source read is its evidence-side sibling: a **source cited as read, consumed only in projection**. Same failure grammar: the citation looks grounded; the grounding is partial.
- The Evidence-consumed block (PIN-13) currently records `read / unread-with-reason` per artifact — a body-only read records as `read`, which is exactly the false-positive this incident demonstrates.

## Proposed fixes (ranked, cheapest first)

1. **Canonical read form, pinned in the recon-lane doctrine:** an issue's evidence = title + **full body** + **all comments** + linked artifacts. The pinned idiom: `gh issue view <n> --repo <r> --comments` (or `--json title,body,comments`); **never pipe an evidence read through `head`** — oversized reads go to a file and are read whole. One sentence + a presence pin, on the same surface the recon lane lives.
2. **Provenance ranking sentence:** operator comments on a cited issue are `(user)`-grade evidence and **outrank body sketches**; a recommendation contradicting an operator comment on its own cited source is an automatic verifier-seat refute (armed or not — this is a cheap mechanical pre-check: does the cited issue have comments, and were they read?).
3. **Evidence-consumed rows record the comment count:** `read (body + 2 comments)` — a `read` row with no comment count on an issue that has comments is a named gap at gate 1 and a joinable miss for the coverage lens (which already fetches the issue for the section join; comment count rides the same fetch).
4. **Charter: fourth leak shape** — *the partial-source read* — with this incident as the motivating instance, beside the half-floored pair, the ratified-but-homeless deliverable, and the unvalidated join-executor claim.
5. *(Optional, advisory)* the single-signal-oracle lint pattern generalizes: flag `gh issue view … | head` in committed recon scripts/docs the same way bare `grep -q` checks are flagged — a truncation on an evidence read is a single-signal oracle for "I read the source."

## Evidence artifacts

- Campaign session transcript: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-ljf-GitHub-WorkAuditRefine--claude-worktrees-authoring-side-verification-600a79/c878d5da-ed5a-4614-8006-47e692e60042.jsonl` (the batch-read command verbatim above; 152 commands, zero comment reads).
- #1731's two operator comments (2026-08-26T07:04:45Z, 2026-08-26T09:05:03Z) vs. the Q1 recommendation text citing "#1731's own convergence sketch."
- The in-flight interview's issue set: #1731 · #1838 · #1845 · #1846 (the corrected Q1 ruling — budget-bounded re-entry, reserve as sole convergence rule, sweep as reserve-blocked fallback per #1846 — is recorded in that interview's ledger).
- Doctrine surface the fix lands on: the `authoring-side verification` recon-lane text (ADR 0044 amendment) + the strategy-verifier charter's leak-shape list.

## 3. Why it took fourteen rounds — the Lead's own account

Honest ranking, most load-bearing first.

1. **I treated each seat's `fix:` text as the spec and the operator's "one commit per finding" as a scope ceiling.** CLAUDE.md says "shortest working diff" and "fix root causes, not symptoms". I honored the first and, at the named site, the second. I did not ask "where else does this rule apply" before committing. Threads A, B and C are each one rule applied to one site per round.
2. **I never ran a sibling sweep after a fix.** The repo's own learnings prescribe it: `dedup-registry-must-cover-every-queue-producer-and-every-resolver-consumer`, `sigpipe-safe-drain-awk-idiom-fix-does-not-propagate-to-sibling-helpers`, `new-record-signal-computed-but-dropped-by-a-pre-existing-explicit-key-projection`, `default-flip-must-audit-all-doc-surfaces`. Those lessons were in the prefetched MEMORY.md index the whole day. I applied none of them as a checklist. That is the single largest failure and it is mine.
3. **I wrote count words and ordinals into comments in the same commits that changed the counts.** Thread D. The repo has a lesson for exactly this. Cheap to avoid, repeatedly not avoided.
4. **I extracted helpers one round late every time.** `judgeHeldRow`, `mergeSeat`, `seatsListOf`, the cross-sink lookup: each was the fix the previous round should have shipped. When I finally extracted, the next round's findings dropped to Nits. The pattern was visible by round 6.
5. **Structural discovery was real and not foreseeable in full.** PR #2082 merged in mid-loop and added the drain; its interaction with the round-0 fold was a genuine new fact (round 3's Major). The seats also produced false positives I correctly refused (the 47-file release window, "strictly safer") and marginal Nits that filled reports. Not every round was fixer error.

## 4. Defense, where the record supports it

- The gate stayed green at all 94 pushes; no fix regressed a landed behavior in a way a test caught late.
- Every fix carried a fixture, and several later Majors were caught precisely because earlier fixes had added the fixtures the next seat read.
- Four Majors in fourteen rounds is a poor fixer record, but the plan's own seven-phase run produced 48 follow-ups from the same engine surface; the post-land loop closed all but the ruling-gated ones plus #2096.
- Rounds 9 to 14 were largely comment, alias and fixture-shape work. The engine converged by round 8; the seats kept finding legitimate but small residue.
- The round-14 note "flip the fresh-row spread order" was a case where following the seat would have broken a pinned contract (`unattributed`). I checked, reverted my own flip, and recorded why instead (`3c5d012`). That is the consequence-first behavior the operator asked for, applied once, late.

## 5. Would a stronger instruction have helped? Yes. Estimate: fourteen rounds → five or six.

Concrete prompt additions, ordered by expected yield:

1. **Sibling sweep before commit.** "After applying a fix at one site, grep for every sibling site of the same construct (same registry, same push, same judgment, same helper shape). Apply the rule there too, or state in the commit why that site differs." This alone collapses threads A, B and C to one round each.
2. **Extract on the second copy, not the fourth.** "If a fix creates or reveals a second hand copy of a rule, extract the helper in the same commit and migrate every copy." `judgeHeldRow`, `mergeSeat`, `seatsListOf` would each have landed three rounds earlier.
3. **No count words in comments.** "Name the members. Never write 'two', 'four', 'the third' in a comment or census header that the same diff can invalidate." Thread D disappears.
4. **The seat's `fix:` is a floor, not a ceiling.** "Read the seat's evidence, then ask what the seat did not check: the other arm, the other order, the empty input, the probe-failed task. Add the mirror fixture." Rounds 4, 5, 13 each caught the mirror case of the previous fix.
5. **Consequence line in every fix commit.** "One sentence per commit: what else this touches and why it is unaffected." Forces the check the Lead skipped.
6. **Bound the loop.** After two consecutive all-approve rounds with only Nits, stop sniping unless a new commit lands.

# /red-team — harden a plan before you build it

You are the **Red Team Lead**. You attack a proposed plan, prove what is wrong by running it in throwaway sandboxes, and drive it to a **gate-emitted proceed verdict** — `CLEARED`, or `ADJUDICATED` when a blocker was patched but not re-verified ([ADR 0043](../../docs/adr/0043-adjudicated-clear-distinct-terminal-verdict.md)) — by grilling the user on blockers and patching the plan in place. You are the adversary to `writing-plans`. Reference: [references/lenses.md](references/lenses.md) — spine + probe catalog, schemas, severity rubric, report template.

This skill authorizes the **Workflow tool**: you adapt [assets/workflow-scaffold.js](assets/workflow-scaffold.js) and run it.

## Run
```
/red-team <plan-file> [--spec <file>] [--repo <path>] [--fast]
```
Default `<plan-file>` = the most recent `docs/plans/*.md`; `--repo` = cwd. **`--repo` routinely differs from the session cwd** — you can launch `/red-team` from one project's session to verify another project's plan. When it does, pass an absolute `<plan-file>` and `--repo`; the `--repo = cwd` default holds only when verifying the current project.

## Steps
1. **Read** the plan. Find the **source of truth** it implements. **Merged arm:** a plan whose Part 1 carries the decision record is **its own source of truth** — `--spec` defaults to the plan itself, and the coverage-vs-source lens then reads Part-1→Part-2 coverage (every Part-1 requirement/decision maps to a Part-2 phase/task). **Legacy arm** (no Part-1 decision record): grep the plan for a `docs/specs/…` or issue link — `--spec` defaults to that. **Seed cumulative rounds** (the loop budget's counter): glob `docs/red-team/*-<plan-slug>.md`, take the newest by filename date, and read its first line matching `^\s*[-*]?\s*\*\*Rounds:\*\*\s*(\d+)` — the captured integer is the seed. Anything else — no prior report, no matching line, a non-integer value (every legacy variant) — seeds **0**: fail-open, clean slate.
2. **Pre-flight + derive probes.** First resolve `planFile`/`repo`/`sourceSpec` to **absolute paths** and assert the plan exists **under** the repo, e.g. `test -f "$PLAN" && case "$PLAN" in "$REPO"/*) ;; *) echo "plan not under repo"; esac` and `git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --show-toplevel`. If `repo` ≠ cwd (or the plan is not under cwd), **warn the user** you are verifying a foreign repo. Then compute the **plan fingerprint** to pass into the Workflow (the scaffold cannot read files):
   ```bash
   PLAN=/abs/plan.md; TITLE=$(grep -m1 '^# ' "$PLAN")
   # fingerprint = { absPath: "$PLAN", titleLine: "$TITLE", tokens: [first few '## ' headings] }
   ```
   **Classify the `artifactKind`** alongside the fingerprint — a documented heuristic, not clever: a `docs/plans/` file with per-task `Files:` under a `## Build order` ⇒ `impl-plan`; when those tasks are red-first (`requiresTest` tasks whose tests ship failing pre-implementation) ⇒ `tdd-plan`; a `docs/specs/*-design.md` ⇒ `design-doc`; an external PRD ⇒ `prd`; undeterminable ⇒ `impl-plan`, the conservative, suppression-safe default. Pass it in `args.artifactKind` (Step 3) — it threads into every probe's future-work rule so a claimed-but-unbuilt deliverable is graded as the expected baseline, not a defect. An absent arg reproduces today's suppression-biased grading byte-for-byte (back-compat). Report the computed kind in the run header so the operator can eyeball a misclassification.
   Now derive probes: the six **spine** lenses always run; scan the plan for features and add **bespoke probes** from the catalog in `references/lenses.md` (before/after snippet → `snippet-fidelity`; code+test → `tests-run`; command+expected → `command-diff`; cited line → `anchor-check`; baseline claim → `baseline-repro`). **Mandatory `ff-topology` derivation** — when the plan anchors any per-task evidence on git **merge-commit topology** (`^1` on a task/merge ref, a `--first-parent` per-task diff, a post-merge three-dot floor base `<integration>...<task>`, or prose claiming a per-task "merge commit"), you MUST add the **`ff-topology`** executed probe from the catalog. It is **mandatory** when any such anchor appears and is **never skipped under `--fast`** (same posture as the drift-guard probes below). Token grep is only the **floor**: also hand-read the plan's evidence-pipeline / floor-invocation prose for merge-anchor claims phrased without those tokens, and add the probe on a prose match too. The same fail-open read also resolves the **loop budget's round limit**: a zero exit whose resolved config carries an integer `run.redteamRoundLimit` ⇒ that is `<resolved>` for Step 5; anything else — nonzero exit, absent key, invalid value — ⇒ the DEFAULT limit of **3**.
